sentences.text: Good morning.

You have three stories today: Nvidia pausing chip server shipments to Southeast Asia, a thousand Claude agents formalizing Fermat's Last Theorem, and the first US utility authorized to build a small modular reactor.
First, the biggest story this morning.
Nvidia has told its server partners to pause shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.
The Journal reports that Dell and Super Micro were told to hold server shipments for an unspecified period.
Nvidia is assessing whether its regional partners are meeting U.S. export requirements.
The reason is that Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers in those countries.
The US Commerce Department closed that loophole earlier this month.
The Institute for Progress estimates those remote data centers supply about 24 percent of China's AI computing power.
I can walk you through how that remote-access loophole worked, if you're curious.
Next, something for your work on agent memory.
Lance Martin, a researcher at Anthropic, describes 1,000 Claude agents formalizing Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean.
The run took about 30 hours and used no domain-specific harness and no human steering on the solution.
The agents' only tools were Git and a SQL database.
The lead agent built database tables to coordinate the team without being told to.
Since you follow agent memory, the coordination tables are the part to hear.
I can tell you what those tables were for, if you'd like.
Now to energy, and small modular reactors.
The Tennessee Valley Authority became the first US power utility authorized to build a commercial small modular reactor, at the end of September.
The project will use the GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 reactor.
Small modular reactors are miniature nuclear reactors built in a factory and assembled on-site.
Over 120 distinct SMR designs have been recorded globally, but many have not achieved licensing.
If you're tracking SMR licensing, this is the one to watch.
I can say more about how the TVA decision fits into the wider picture, if you're interested.
Which of these would you like to dig into?
